_global.note: STOP before doing WordPress-{state} selector work. Measured 2026-08-05 with scripts/find-duplicate-library-urls.js: 355 domains are shared across two or more ACTIVE states, covering 1073 of the ~4069 configured library entries. The seed data was generated by guessing '{city}library.org' from the city name, so madisonlibrary.org is assigned to libraries in 11 states, greenvillelibrary.org in 10, franklinlibrary.org in 10. A domain can be the real site of at most one of them. Until the URLs are corrected, a scraper returning 0 events may simply be pointed at another state's library — and broadening extraction would ingest that other library's events under the wrong name and state. Fix URLs before selectors. General discipline: read SCRAPER-FIX-LOG.jsonl first, verify claims before acting, run `node -c` on every modified scraper, and append one line per logical fix to SCRAPER-FIX-LOG.jsonl. SECOND SEED-DATA DEFECT, measured 2026-08-05: the same generator also fabricated county names by appending ' County' to the city ('Arcadia County', 'Brandon County', 'Archer County' -- none are real counties). Across the 20 active WordPress-{state} library files, 2065 of 2137 county values (96.6%) fail getCountyCentroid() lookup; only 72 resolve. Worst: NY 416 bad, MA 231, PA 206, NJ 166; VT/TN/KY/MS/WV are 100% bad. Effect: the county-centroid tier of the geocoding chain is effectively dead for this entire family, so any library whose address/city geocode fails lands on the STATE centroid. This is the same class of work as the URL remediation and needs a real city-to-county data source -- do not guess counties one at a time. ADDED 2026-08-07: two cross-cutting items intentionally NOT queued as ordinary daily fix work, because CLAUDE.md's Scraper Naming rules explicitly say not to open a mass renaming campaign from a daily diagnosis, and because the verification backlog below is too large for incidental fixing: (1) SCRAPER-NAME CONFORMANCE — 315 of 464 distinct scraper_name values (68%) still drift from the two legal forms in CLAUDE.md, essentially flat versus the prior baseline (not a regression, just proportional growth). Two scrapers are COLLAPSED (MacaroniKid-MD: 20 sites under 1 name; MacaroniKid-DE: 2 sites under 1 name) and need per-site slugs first since collapsing violates the no-aggregation rule. A full remediation is a deliberate, scoped migration project the project owner should explicitly greenlight (likely phased by scraper family, largest offenders first), not something to execute piecemeal from this file. (2) VERIFICATION BACKLOG — 254 pre-existing UNVERIFIABLE zero-event library rows from prior audit cycles (bot-blocks, JS-only widgets, timeouts) have never been re-checked; a dedicated task chip was spawned for this (title: 'Re-verify 254 UNVERIFIABLE zero-event library sites') rather than attempting it inside a daily run — pick it up as its own session when convenient, batching WebFetch checks across parallel subagents per the Step 3d pattern. PLATFORM-MISMATCH GROUP, identified 2026-08-10 by browser re-probe, NOT yet fixed. These libraries do not publish events on their own site at all - the events live on another platform, so no amount of selector work on the WordPress DOM path can reach them. Each needs relocating to the right family scraper with its correct per-library URL, exactly the move made for Auburn Public Library (WordPress-GA to LibCal-GA). LibCal: Greenwich Library (CT), City Of Bayou La Batre (AL), Kenton County (KY), Chester Springs (PA), Erie County (PA). BiblioCommons: Avalon, Community Library Of Castle Shannon, Clairton, Coraopolis (all PA). Communico: Dudley Branch (MA). FullCalendar: Shaw Public Library Greenville (ME). Deliberately left configured rather than removed - the library is real and only its platform assignment is wrong, so removing would lose genuine coverage instead of relocating it.

AGE-YEARPAIR-MISREAD.note: NOT a registry scraper — a cross-cutting finding kept visible in the Fix queue. OPEN, ongoing deletion of children's events. Distinct from the resolveAgeRange 'Adults' fix that landed 2026-08-13: that one gave a supplied 'Adults' a second opinion from the title and rescued 285 wrongly-deleted event instances, but it CANNOT rescue this class because the title itself yields no valid non-adult signal. Symptom: a title containing a YEAR PAIR or similar numeric pair is read as an age range, resolves to Adults, and the event is deleted. Largest known victim is '2026-27 KidsPlex After-School (Pay-by-Day Option)' with 82 rejected instances in scraper-stdout.log — a school-year label 2026-27 parsed as ages 26-27. This is the same family of false positive CLAUDE.md already documents for registration IDs ('2608-2026' read as 8-20) and times ('1:00 - 2:30p' read as 0-2), which is why normalizeAgeRange must never be fed a raw title. The remaining gap is that a numeric pair reaching detectAgeRange/normalizeAgeRange through a SUPPLIED value is still trusted. Suggested direction, NOT yet implemented or verified: reject an age range parsed from a pair that looks like a year or school year (both parts >= 1900, or a 4-digit first part, or a YYYY-YY shape) before it can normalize to Adults. Measure first — run the 320 distinct titles in scraper-stdout.log through any candidate change and check both directions, since the 968 not-rescued instances are a MIXED bag containing genuinely adult events (Coffee & Conversation, 3D Printer Orientation) that must stay rejected. Extend scripts/test-age-detection.js with the year-pair cases plus adult controls before shipping.

STABLE-ID-COLLISIONS.note: NOT a registry scraper — a cross-cutting finding kept visible in the Fix queue. ACTIVE, ONGOING DATA LOSS, found 2026-08-12/13 in the catch-up Group 2 run. Six scrapers emitted 🚨 STABLE-ID COLLISION warnings, meaning two genuinely different events hashed to the same row id so only one survives and the rest are silently dropped. Root cause is always the same: the scraper puts a SHARED url (a library homepage or calendar page) on every event instead of a per-event link, and _stableEventId hashes the url first. Exact attribution from that run — LibCal-CT / Hamden Public Library ('Time For Twos Storytime' vs 'Garden Club'); LibCal-PA / Easton Area Public Library ('Card Club' vs 'Lunch at the Library'); LibCal-TN / Clarksville-Montgomery County Public Library ('North Branch Toddler Craft Time' vs 'North Branch Toddler Time Story Time'); Berks-County ('Toddler Storytime' vs "Children's Storytime"); Rockbridge-Regional ('Tech Power Hour' vs 'Book Sale Set-up'); CustomDrupal-Libraries / Kanawha County Public Library ('The Sci-Fi/Fantasy Hour' vs "Let's talk programming"). NOTE these six are only the collisions that were DETECTABLE — the warning fires when two differently-named events collide inside one run, so the true loss is a floor, not a total. DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED IN THAT SESSION, and the reason matters: the correct fix is either to extract a real per-event URL or to pin identity to name|eventDate|venue (the pattern already used for WithApps-Libraries and RollyPollies-MD), but BOTH change _stableEventId for every event the scraper produces, so every existing row would re-insert under a new id and duplicate. That blast radius needs a deliberate, verified, per-scraper pass with live DOM inspection — not a blind six-file edit at the end of a long session. Do the LibCal trio together if possible: LibCal event pages normally DO have per-event URLs, so those three are likely a missing extraction rather than a genuinely shared page.

WordPress-GA.note: Banks County Public Library moved out to LibCal-GA on 2026-08-05 (was on homerlibrary.org = Homer Glen ILLINOIS; the real library uses LibCal via Piedmont Regional). STILL OPEN in this file: Greenville Area Public Library remains on greenvillelibrary.org, which is the South Carolina county system - one of 8 active states still claiming that domain and needing individual URL research. Also part of the known WordPress platform-heterogeneity problem: each library runs a different theme, so there is no generic selector patch. Confirm the URL is the right institution before blaming extraction. RESOLVED 2026-08-08: New Georgia Public Library repointed to wgrls.org (West Georgia Regional Library System), verified live as the real institution. wgrls.org 403-blocks the TEC REST API (tryFetchTecEvents returns null), so the generic DOM fallback was grabbing the TEC list view's day-heading wrapper elements instead of real events — 0 real events had ever saved for this library, and 56 junk rows (bare date strings as titles) had accumulated. Fixed properly, not just patched: added tryDomScrapeTecEvents() to tec-rest-helper.js, which targets TEC v2's actual list-view markup (.tribe-events-calendar-list__event, its title-link, the datetime attribute, venue title/address, description) directly rather than guessing generic selectors, and wired it into scraper-wordpress-libraries-ga.js as a fallback tried between the REST call and the fully-generic DOM scrape. Confirmed live: 10 real events with real titles/dates/times/descriptions extracted from wgrls.org, 5 saved on the first re-run (others were future-dated beyond the window or filtered elsewhere), all carrying correct venue, source_url, and distinct per-event URLs. Two junk-title patterns (added earlier the same day) remain in place as a second line of defense for any other TEC site whose REST API is also blocked. This helper function isn't GA-specific — any other WordPress-{state} file already wired to tryFetchTecEvents (NY/FL/NJ/MS/ME/NC/CT/TN/AL/VT) could use the same fallback if it hits the same 403-blocked-REST-but-live-HTML situation; not retrofitted elsewhere this session, scoped to the library actually being fixed. Ruth Enlow (Garrett) and Kent County were added and both work: 3 and 22 events. Four guessed /events paths were replaced with real calendar URLs found on each library's own site. Two entries were REMOVED as verified-covered-elsewhere: Queen Anne's (33 DB rows from calendar.qaclibrary.org) whose /events served a Squarespace 404, and Washington County Free (28 rows from wcfl.librarymarket.com). OUTCOME: found rose 163 to 310, but NEW only 82 to 80 and INVALID rose 6 to 135. The URL fixes surfaced an extraction bug rather than adding saved events. ST MARY'S IS THE WHOLE STORY: its corrected URL now returns 147 events, but the generic WordPress selectors grab the time field as the date ('10 a.m.', '9:30 a.m.', '2:30 p.m.Registration'), so nearly all fail date parsing. St Mary's is also configured in Communico-MD at stmalib.libnet.info/events, which is the right parser for its LibNet platform - but Communico-MD produces ZERO St Mary's rows, so it cannot simply be removed here. Fixing Communico-MD for St Mary's is the correct path; until then WordPress-MD keeps the entry and the INVALID count is a true signal, not noise. STILL ZERO: Somerset County (somelibrary.org/events.php returns nothing). NEAR ZERO: Charles County 1, Dorchester 1 - both are real pages whose events are JS-rendered or on a separate platform (Charles is Communico at ccplonline.libnet.info). RESOLVED 2026-08-07: St. Mary's and Charles County were removed from this scraper because Communico-MD demonstrably covers both - verified by watching its run produce 5 rows for each. INVALID fell from 135 to 5 and saved events held at 79 (was 80), confirming the 147 St. Mary's events had never been saving. Remaining: Somerset County still returns 0. SOMERSET DIAGNOSED 2026-08-07 (not fixable by this scraper): somelibrary.org/events.php has a body of only 493 characters and no dates - all its events live in TWO EMBEDDED GOOGLE CALENDAR IFRAMES covering five calendar IDs. No DOM scraper can reach cross-origin iframe content, so this entry will return 0 forever. The events ARE reachable: each calendar exposes a public ICS feed at https://calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/<ID>%40group.calendar.google.com/public/basic.ics, verified 2026-08-07 returning HTTP 200 with 468KB and 152KB of real VEVENT data. The five IDs are somelibrary.org_jh8uo8466kov1vth331eje1t7s, _91sbe6asf4phciq8lcn2rlaf1k, _gcd8aeg949e1f9aobi8j418ab8, _qkhpuchqt21ec8sic3fu9chveo and _9871gfpt9lofa0cotrpciutcsg. node-ical is already a dependency (scraper-pratt-library-MD.js uses it). Implementing this needs an ICS extraction path and a filter for upcoming events, since the feeds carry history back to 2022 - it is a new capability, not a URL fix, so it was recorded rather than bolted onto a DOM scraper. SOMERSET RESOLVED 2026-08-07: removed from this scraper and now covered by the new GoogleCalendar-MD, which reads the five ICS feeds behind its Google Calendar iframes - 126 events saved, 0 invalid. WordPress-MD is now 7 entries and every Maryland library is either producing events, covered by its correct platform scraper, or has a recorded verified reason.

Dorchester-County.note: FIXED 2026-08-10. Reported "Found 12, New 12" on every run while writing ZERO rows for months. Root cause was not in this scraper: _stableEventId() in supabase-adapter.js hashed a query-stripped URL, and Google Calendar htmlLinks carry their identity entirely in ?eid=, so every Google-Calendar event in the fleet collapsed onto ONE row id. The id this scraper kept colliding on was owned by Somerset County Library/Crisfield. Adapter now folds non-tracking query params into the hash; URLs without a query string hash unchanged, so no id churn elsewhere. Confirmed live: 0 -> 12 rows here, 0 -> 153 for Somerset-County. This scrapers success logging also now counts {duplicate:true} as skipped rather than imported - the same miscount exists in other .add()-path scrapers and was NOT swept.

Identity now pinned to name|eventDate|venue. Also set metadata.scraperName to the registry key; rows had been landing under the display name "Hampton Public Library" and could not be joined to the registry. Live after fix: 37 rows. RollyPollies-MD.note: FIXED 2026-08-10. url is a ternary between two booking-landing pages, so all events collapsed onto at most two ids - claimed 20 new with 1 row present. Identity pinned to name|eventDate|venue and the duplicate return is no longer counted as an import. Live after fix: 10 rows, and a clean re-run now honestly reports 34 found / 0 new / 34 duplicates. The gap between 20 claimed and 10 stored is the schema: idx_events_unique_content is on name+event_date+venue, so two same-named sessions on one day cannot both exist regardless of id. Distinguishing them would need the schema changed to include start_time - not attempted.

supabase-adapter.js.note: Not a registry scraper — a shared-infra note so this stays visible in the Fix queue. Two fleet-wide changes landed 2026-08-10, both awaiting their first full rotation. (1) STABLE-ID: _stableEventId now folds non-tracking query params into the row-id hash. Previously the entire query string was stripped, so every Google-Calendar htmlLink collapsed to one id fleet-wide and only the first event of each source ever saved. URLs with no query string hash unchanged, so no id churn is expected anywhere else — if a scraper suddenly reports a large jump in NEW with no site change, check that its URLs carry query params before assuming a regression. (2) MISCOUNT: 96 of 96 .add() call sites now treat a {duplicate:true} return as skipped rather than imported. Re-measure both with scripts/audit-add-miscount.js and scripts/verify-duplicate-branch-scope.js.
